(ריב"ש סימן רכ"ו):
mechaber.en:
דין צרכי רבים בחול המועד. ובו ב סעיפים:
1. The Laws of Public Needs During Chol HaMoed, 2 Seifim: It is permitted on Chol HaMoed to take care of the needs of the community, such as fixing roads and removing stumbling blocks (or obstacles) from them, and to mark (or point out) graves so the priests can be warned about them, and to fix the Mikvahs. RAMA: Specifically public needs like needs for the person's body (or well being) but other public needs, like building a synagogue (Beis Yosef in the name of the Teshuvos HaRashbah) are forbidden to do during Chol HaMoed. And this is the law for other mitzvah related needs - it is forbidden to perform artistic work during Chold HaMoed (Rivash, Siman 226). ):

ס"א ודוקא כו'. כמש"ש ומנין שאם לא יצאו ועשו כו' ובתוספתא פ"ק חומת העיר שנפרצה גודרין אותה גדרה ונפרצה אין גודרין אותה אם היתה סמוכה לספר סותרה ובונה כדרכה אלמא לא התירו אלא משום סכנה וזש"ש אפי' להגיה כו' ואלו כותבין כו' דכ"ז צרכי רבים הן לגופם וכמ"ש הרמב"ם משא"כ בס"ת דאינו צרכי גוף דלא כמ"ש בסי' תקמ"ה ס"ב ומה שדקדק מרמב"ם שם אין מוכרח דה"ק דכל כתיבת ס"ת והגהתה הכל אינו צרכי רבים כנ"ל וז"ש אפי' בספר עזרה ומשמע דשולל הכל וקאמר אלו כותבין דוקא אלו אבל לא ס"ת:
וה"ה דלשאר כו'. ממש"ש ו' א' דטעמא דיוצאין על הכלאים משום שכר פעולה כו':
beur_hagra.en:
Seif 1, and specifically, etc. As written there: from where do we know that if they did not go out and do, etc. And in the Tosefta, first chapter: a city wall that was breached, they repair it; if it was repaired and breached again, they do not repair it. If it was near the border, he demolishes and builds in the usual manner. Thus they permitted only because of danger. This is what is written there, "even to correct," etc., and "these may be written," etc., for all these are public needs for their bodies, as Rambam wrote. This is unlike a Sefer Torah, which is not a bodily need, not like what is written in siman 545 seif 2. What he inferred from Rambam there is not compelling; this is what he means: all writing of a Sefer Torah and correcting it is not public need, as appears to me. This is what he wrote, "even a scroll of Ezra," implying that he excludes all of it, and then says "these may be written," specifically these but not a Sefer Torah.
The same applies to other, etc. From what is written there 6a, that the reason they go out regarding kilayim is because of the wage for labor, etc.

(ז) לעשות במועד - כתב בשערי תשובה נהגו לסדר צרכי רבים בח"ה למנות גבאים ופרנסים. ונ"ל דאם צריך לכתוב בענין זה לא יכתוב כתב אשורית כ"א משיט"א או כתב שלנו דבכתב אשורי שהוא מעשה אומן הלא לא הותר צרכי רבים כ"א כשהוא לצורך הגוף וכנ"ל:

turei_zahav.en: And likewise for other mitzvah needs. Beit Yosef at the end of this siman brings the words of Tosafot on what the Gemara says: they go out for kilayim on the festival because then workers are hired cheaply, and Tosafot challenged the one who says worker's pay when he has nothing to eat is forbidden — how can they hire workers? And they answered: perhaps one could say that these of mitzvah they permitted. And Beit Yosef wrote on this: and even though we hold like the one who says worker's pay is permitted when he has nothing to eat, nevertheless one can learn that where it was for mitzvah need, even if the worker has what to eat, it is permitted — end of his words. And this contradicts what the Rama wrote here regarding other mitzvah needs that it is forbidden, and this is from the words of Ribash whom Beit Yosef brings. And at first glance it appears to me to distinguish that specifically on the moed, even though it is incumbent on the person to do it, nevertheless he can do it after the festival — in this it is forbidden, and on Chol Hamoed one sits idle. But where there is a prohibition on the person to sit idle, such as the case of kilayim where one who maintains kilayim is lashed — certainly it is permitted to hire a worker even if he has what to eat. However a question arises on this from what is written in the siman after that one does not proofread even one letter, and behold there is a prohibition because of "do not place an obstacle in your tent" — and therefore it appears to me that one should not learn from these words of Tosafot permission for mitzvah, and their question it appears to me to answer that going out for kilayim is public needs, for the tanna counted it among the other public needs at the beginning of Moed Katan in the mishnah, and through this it is permitted as written in the seif after. Also Tosafot did not write their reasoning except by way of "perhaps"; but from the words of the Tur in the siman after it is proven that mitzvah is permitted — see there.
